name: Zuo Shang (prologue duel)
summary: Zuo Shang (prologue duel) is a story (tutorial) encounter in Prologue & Weeping Creek Valley, found at Opening pursuit sequence.

Dying here costs nothing, so use it to learn what a red flash feels like before it matters.

name: The Hunt
summary: The Hunt is a story encounter in Prologue & Weeping Creek Valley, found at Main road pursuit, returns later. Beating it yields Hunter's Chain Sickle (Great Waterfall, same region).
drops: Hunter's Chain Sickle (Great Waterfall, same region)
tips: Learn his attack rhythm first; the punish window is after the follow-up, not after the first swing.
He returns later in the story at a higher level, so the early fight doubles as a rehearsal.

Guard breaks land faster than chip damage here; he armours through light hits.

Break his guard with Sha-Chi attacks to take the Dread Axe.

name: Hua, Deadly Betrothed (新娘阿花)

tips: Do not stand in the Flesh Lily fields - they explode on a delay and the tell is easy to miss while dodging her.
Her grab is unblockable; the dodge window is late, after she commits.

name: Aberrant Three-Faced Puppet
summary: Aberrant Three-Faced Puppet is a optional encounter in Prologue & Weeping Creek Valley, found at Challenge Rift.
tips: An optional Challenge Rift fight - bring upgraded gear rather than attempting it early.
Each face changes the attack set, so re-read the silhouette after every phase change.

name: The Gold-Masked One
summary: The Gold-Masked One is a recurring optional encounter in Prologue & Weeping Creek Valley, found at Lóng Pillar trials, five times.

He escalates each meeting; do not assume the pattern from the previous fight still holds.

He is the boss most likely to teach you that mashing loses to patience.

name: Jing Ye, the Outlaw (亡命徒 荆野)
summary: Jing Ye, the Outlaw (亡命徒 荆野) is a story encounter in Crimson Manor & Crimson Forest, found at Crimson Forest. Beating it yields Outlaw Warblade.
tips: Dodge the mounted charges rather than trying to block them, and punish between attack sequences.

Reward is the Iron Gauntlets, which change how the next few fights feel.

summary: Bai Chilian, Lady of the Twin Serpents (双蛇夫人 白赤练) is a story - region finale encounter in Crimson Manor & Crimson Forest, found at Threadbound Great Tree, after the mirror puzzle. Beating it yields White Serpent & Crimson Viper.

Keep one blade's stamina in reserve for the phase change.

summary: Jade Dancer and Iron Fiend is a optional encounter in Crimson Manor & Crimson Forest, found at Crimson Forest. Beating it yields Fiend Saws (via the Mu Xiaokui encounter).
drops: Fiend Saws (via the Mu Xiaokui encounter)

Kill order matters more than damage output here.

Dropped into the puppet well after both Bi fights.

name: Gu Wanyue (女妖 骨婉约)
summary: Gu Wanyue (女妖 骨婉约) is a story encounter in Pangzhen, found at The Singing Pond bell.
tips: She is immune to damage until her Sha-Chi bar breaks; parries and perfect dodges are the only way to drain it.
Deflect the blue-flash projectile back at her - it marks her and opens the biggest window.
Dodge every red-flash grab, especially the handstand neck-breaker; a clean dodge removes a large chunk of her bar.
When the arena goes dark she can attack from any angle: hold block and react to the flash rather than parrying blind.

phases.answer: Parry - this is the main Sha-Chi drain
Perfect parry to deflect it back; applies vulnerability

phases.watch: Handstand leap onto your shoulders, red flash
phases.answer: Dodge - removes a large chunk of her bar
Hold block, react to the flash, do not parry blind

strategy: Gu Wanyue is the fight that teaches the game's defensive loop, because for most of it she cannot be damaged at all: while the smoke effect is on her body, attacks pass through. The only way in is to empty her Sha-Chi bar, and the only way to empty it is to parry and dodge correctly.

The rhythm is drain, stagger, burst: parry the sleeve strings, deflect the projectile, dodge the grabs, then unload everything the moment she staggers. Back off the instant she recovers and start again. Healing before the arena, not during it, is the difference between a clean attempt and a wipe.

summary: Xie Qiudong, the Divine Healer (神医 谢秋冬) is a story encounter in Pangzhen, found at Up from the Three Ships Well.

name: Wu Lengshuang, the Soft Sword (柔剑 武林霜)
summary: Wu Lengshuang, the Soft Sword (柔剑 武林霜) is a optional encounter in Mandate Encampment, found at Path of the Baishan's Fall. Beating it yields Soft Snake Sword.
tips: Stop attacking the moment the purple flash appears - that is her parry, and a counter is already coming.
Dodge when the follow-up glints red, parry when it glints blue.
Her only two-handed swing is always followed by an unblockable spinning slash.
The acrobatic forward flip slash is parryable and is her main gap closer.

phases.answer: Dodge the red, parry the blue

phases.watch: Only attack she uses two hands for
phases.answer: Always followed by an unblockable spin - dodge it
Parryable - this is your Ghoststep opening

strategy: Wu Lengshuang is a parry duel rather than a damage race. She deflects constantly, and every deflection is a purple flash that cancels your damage and leads straight into a counter whose colour tells you what to do: red means dodge, blue means parry, no colour means block or reposition.
The mistake that loses this fight is pressing through the purple flash. Treat it as a stop signal, react to the counter, and take the acrobatic flip slash as your one reliable Ghoststep opening.

name: Zuo Shang, The True Long
summary: Zuo Shang, The True Long is a story - final boss encounter in Mount Soulrend & endgame, found at Peak of Mount Soulrend. Beating it yields Aureate.
tips: High burst damage is the answer: chill him with Whiteshadow, then swap to Blazing Edge once he is guard-broken or frozen.
You Loong's Deluge staggers him flat, which is the most reliable way to control the pace of the fight.
In phase 1, when he turns his back he is either throwing a spinning sword or setting a counter-parry - do not swing blindly.
Phase 2 is a defensive fight: block and parry the melee, evade the projectiles, and wait for the Sha-Chi break instead of forcing damage.

phases.watch: A swarm of swords fills the arena
phases.answer: Spam dodge - do not try to parry it

phases.watch: Red flash while wind and leaves gather
Five swords fire in sequence, then a leap
phases.answer: Parry the sword swing, dodge the grab that follows
Unblockable thrust - dodge sideways, not back
Expect a spinning projectile or a counter-parry - hold your swing

strategy: The true-ending final boss is a two-phase exam on everything the game has taught. Phase 1 is readable: he telegraphs, and the back-turned stance is a trap rather than an opening. Phase 2 removes the luxury of forcing damage - his poise is high enough that reckless combos get punished, so the fight becomes block, parry, evade until the Sha-Chi bar breaks, then a single committed burst.

The build that makes it tractable is a freeze into burst swap: Whiteshadow to chill and slow him, Blazing Edge for the damage window once he is frozen or guard-broken, with You Loong's Deluge available to knock him down when the pressure needs resetting.

name: The Last Battle
